final_message:
I reproduced the bug at 4f08332 (eslint 9.14.0, which uses @eslint/config-array 0.18.0), so it's still there at this revision.

This machine runs Linux, so I simulated Windows: the script loads ESLint, then switches Node's shared `path` module to `path.win32` (the behaviour Node has on Windows). It uses cwd `C:\Project` and checks three files with three APIs:

| File | FlatConfigArray status | Linter#verify | ESLint#lintText (`--no-config-lookup`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `C:\Project\foo.js` | matched (ok) | linted (ok) | linted (ok) |
| `C:\Other\foo.js` | external (ok) | "No matching configuration found" (ok) | "File ignored because outside of base path." (ok) |
| `F:\foo.js` | **matched** | **no-undef reported** | **no-undef reported** |

Run it with `node repro/windows-cross-drive.js`. It exits with code 1 while the bug is present. The script is `repro/windows-cross-drive.js`.

**Likely cause:** the problem seems to be in `@eslint/config-array`, not in eslint's own code. `getConfigWithStatus` treats a file as outside the base path only if `path.relative(this.basePath, filePath)` starts with `".."` (in `node_modules/@eslint/config-array/dist/cjs/index.cjs`, around line 953). On Windows, the relative path between two different drives isn't relative at all: `path.relative("C:\\Project", "F:\\foo.js")` returns the absolute `"F:\\foo.js"`. So the check never fires, and the file falls through to the normal `**/*.js` matching. The script prints both `path.relative` results at the top. The same `startsWith("..")` check also appears in `shouldIgnorePath` and `isDirectoryIgnored`.

**Limitation:** I didn't run the actual CLI file-path route (`lintFiles` on `F:\foo.js`). It needs a real second drive, so it can't run here. `lintText` with `filePath` goes through the same ignore check.
